sources.title: Government review of the electronic-visa project
sources.publisher: Government of the Republic of Equatorial Guinea Information and Press Office
sources.officialityEvidence: The Government's 15 April 2026 publication confirms that the national online-visa project is operating, reports approvals through March 2026, and identifies the Foreigners Directorate and VFS Global as its operators.
sources.supportingExcerpt: desde julio de 2023 hasta marzo de 2026, se han aprobado 28.479 visados

sources.title: Equatorial Guinea eVisa: nationality eligibility
sources.officialityEvidence: This live VFS service asset says the service is provided by VFS Global on behalf of Equatorial Guinea's Ministry of Foreign Affairs. The Government's current April 2026 publication separately identifies VFS Global as operator of the national online-visa project; the asset expresses general all-nationality availability.
sources.supportingExcerpt: All Nationalities can apply for an E- Visa

sources.title: Equatorial Guinea eVisa: regular-passport document scope
sources.officialityEvidence: The same live VFS eVisa asset says the service is provided on behalf of Equatorial Guinea's Ministry of Foreign Affairs and explicitly limits the online application to a regular passport; it also requires use of the same passport for travel.
sources.supportingExcerpt: The only travel document that can be used in the E-Visa application process is your regular passport.

sources.title: Equatorial Guinea eVisa: email and PDF decision delivery
sources.officialityEvidence: The current live VFS service asset says it is provided on behalf of Equatorial Guinea's Ministry of Foreign Affairs and identifies online registration, payment, and electronic pre-travel delivery. Its HTTP Last-Modified value is 30 July 2026, and the Government's April 2026 report confirms continued operation.
sources.supportingExcerpt: All E-Visa are sent by email, to the email address informed at the time of registration.

sources.title: Chamber of Deputies ratifies several cooperation agreements
sources.publisher: Government of the Republic of Equatorial Guinea Information and Press Office
sources.officialityEvidence: This accessible Government report is historical, not current-force proof. It reports Tunisia's unilateral waiver for Equatoguineans and the President's stated will that Equatorial Guinea reciprocate for up to 90 days.
sources.supportingExcerpt: manifestó su voluntad de que la parte ecuatoguineana actúe en reciprocidad

sources.title: Foreign Minister's Senate hearing on the Tunisia visa-waiver agreement
sources.publisher: Government of the Republic of Equatorial Guinea Information and Press Office
sources.officialityEvidence: This accessible Government report is historical, not current-force proof. It describes the then-discussed agreement as covering diplomatic, official and service passports and says no official document had been signed at that time.
sources.supportingExcerpt: cuando hasta la fecha no se tiene un documento oficial firmado por ambos países

unresolved.reason: Current Government eVisa sources establish an operating online option for regular passports and electronic delivery, but do not identify Tunisia as visa-liable, exclude a Tunisian ordinary passport from a waiver, or state that any waiver ended. The accessible historical Government reporting is not current-force proof: its 2018 account records only the President's will to reciprocate up to 90 days, while its 2019 account describes a then-unsigned convention for diplomatic, official and service passports. No current primary law, revocation, exclusion or Tunisia-specific controlling route was directly accessible. eVisa availability is context, not a basis to replace the fallback visa_free hypothesis.
